prompt:
You are a credit rating analyst. Using only the information below and general knowledge predating 2026-04-22, assign the issuer a letter credit rating on the 21-grade scale below (finest granularity you can justify).
Valid answers (choose exactly one): AAA, AA+, AA, AA-, A+, A, A-, BBB+, BBB, BBB-, BB+, BB, BB-, B+, B, B-, CCC+, CCC, CCC-, CC, C.
Company information (as of 2026-04-22):
| Current ratio           | 1.18 |
| Retained earnings       | 17,162M |
| Current liabilities     | 105,547M |
| Current assets          | 124,141M |
| Shareholders' equity    | 5,987M |
| Total liabilities       | 158,800M |
| Total assets            | 164,787M |
| EBIT / operating income | 446M |
| Revenue                 | 22,217M |
Reason briefly in 1-3 sentences. Then, on a separate final line, output exactly:
DECISION: <one label>
raw_response:
The company shows very high leverage with equity of only 5,987M against 158,800M in liabilities and 164,787M in assets, leaving a tiny equity cushion. EBIT is modest relative to the scale of debt, suggesting limited interest coverage and higher default risk, with a current ratio around 1.18 indicating limited liquidity headroom. Overall, credit risk appears well into the non-investment-grade territory.

DECISION: CCC+
